1	# Ultra Sound Money: Ethereum's Post-Merge Supply Dynamics
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://ultrasound.money/
     5	
     6	## Current Supply Overview
     7	
     8	As of the latest data, Ethereum's total supply stands at **121,603,980 ETH**, with a price of **$2,243 USD** and base gas fees at a historic low of **0.1 Gwei**. Over the trailing 7-day period, the network added a net **+19,445.89 ETH** to supply, translating to an annualized growth rate of **+0.83%/year**. This net figure results from **19,638.29 ETH issued** to validators minus only **192.39 ETH burned** through EIP-1559 base fee destruction — an issuance offset ratio of just **0.01x**, meaning burns currently offset only ~1% of new issuance.
     9	
    10	The burn rate is suppressed by historically low gas prices. The 7-day gas market shows a minimum of 0.0 Gwei, maximum of 1.3 Gwei, and average of just 0.1 Gwei — well below the levels needed for deflationary supply dynamics. Blob gas (introduced via EIP-4844 for L2 data availability) averaged 7,144,934 wei with a total blob fee burn of only 0.15 ETH ($319) over 7 days.
    11	
    12	## Burn Categories and Leaderboard (7-Day)
    13	
    14	| Category | Burn (ETH) |
    15	|---|---|
    16	| DeFi | 31 |
    17	| ETH transfers | 22 |
    18	| Misc | 4 |
    19	| NFTs | 3 |
    20	| Contract creations | 2 |
    21	| L2 | 0 |
    22	| MEV | 0 |
    23	| Blob fees | 0 |
    24	| **Total** | **~192 ETH** |
    25	
    26	The burn leaderboard is led by ETH transfers (21.74 ETH), Tether USDT (13.55 ETH), and various DeFi contracts. Recent blocks (e.g., 24,850,874–24,850,879) show burns of 0.00–0.01 ETH per block, reflecting the extremely low fee environment. The 7-day burn record was just 0.07 ETH in a single block.
    27	
    28	## Staking and Validator Economics
    29	
    30	Ethereum's proof-of-stake system currently has **38.9M ETH staked** (~32% of supply). The scarcity engine locks 9.1M ETH in staking contracts with an average time span of 10.7 years. Validator rewards break down as:
    31	
    32	| Reward Type | Amount | APR |
    33	|---|---|---|
    34	| Issuance | 0.9 ETH/validator | 2.7% |
    35	| Tips | 0.0 ETH | 0.1% |
    36	| MEV estimate | 0.0 ETH | 0.1% |
    37	| **Total** | | **~2.9%** |
    38	
    39	PoS issuance runs at approximately **2,800 ETH/day**, while fee burn at current gas levels is roughly **2,200 ETH/day** under normalized assumptions (though the 7-day actual burn is far lower).
    40	
    41	## Supply Projections and Equilibrium
    42	
    43	The 200-year supply projection models ETH converging to an equilibrium of **125.7M ETH**, assuming 39M ETH staked and a 22 Gwei average base gas price. At equilibrium, issuance and burn balance at approximately **1,037K ETH/year**. The issuance rewards rate for stakers is 2.7%/year, while the effective burn rate for non-stakers is 1.2%/year.
    44	
    45	![ETH Supply 2Y Projection](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    46	
    47	The 2-year projection chart shows Ethereum's supply history across eras: genesis (5 ETH/block), Byzantium (3 ETH/block), Constantinople (2 ETH/block), phase 0 staking, London burn introduction, and the merge (PoW removal). Supply growth has flattened dramatically post-merge.
    48	
    49	## Flippening Progress and Total Value Secured
    50	
    51	ETH's market cap relative to competing monetary assets:
    52	
    53	| Asset | ETH Market Cap Ratio |
    54	|---|---|
    55	| Bitcoin | 18.70% |
    56	| USD | 1.30% |
    57	| Gold | 0.89% |
    58	
    59	Total Value Secured (TVS) on Ethereum:
    60	
    61	| Category | Value (USD) |
    62	|---|---|
    63	| ETH (native) | $272.76B |
    64	| ERC20 tokens | $22.21B |
    65	| NFTs | $12.66B |
    66	| **Total** | **~$307.6B** |
    67	
    68	Top ERC20s by value include Dai ($4.41B), Shiba Inu ($3.51B), Cronos ($2.97B), and Tether Gold ($2.65B). Top NFT collections include CryptoPunks ($2.13B), Bored Ape Yacht Club ($0.68B), ENS ($0.63B), and Pudgy Penguins ($0.51B).
    69	
    70	The community ("fam") counts 6,000+ members tracking these metrics.
    71	
    72	![Flippening Dashboard](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    73	
    74	## Key Findings
    75	
    76	- **ETH is currently mildly inflationary** at +0.83%/year due to historically low gas fees (avg 0.1 Gwei), with burns offsetting only ~1% of issuance over the past 7 days.
    77	- **DeFi and ETH transfers dominate burn activity**, accounting for roughly 85% of the 192 ETH burned in the trailing week, but absolute burn volumes are negligible at current gas levels.
    78	- **38.9M ETH (32% of supply) is staked**, creating a significant supply lock with validators earning ~2.7% APR primarily from protocol issuance rather than tips or MEV.
    79	- **Long-term equilibrium is projected at 125.7M ETH**, requiring sustained ~22 Gwei average gas to balance issuance and burn at ~1,037K ETH/year — the ultra sound money thesis depends on on-chain activity recovery.
    80	- **Ethereum secures over $307B in total value** and has reached 18.7% of Bitcoin's market cap, demonstrating growing but still early monetary premium.

     2	name: ppt-master
     3	description: >
     4	  AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents
     5	  (PDF/DOCX/URL/Markdown) into high-quality SVG pages and exports to PPTX through
     6	  multi-role collaboration. Use when user asks to "create PPT", "make presentation",
     7	  "生成PPT", "做PPT", "制作演示文稿", or mentions "ppt-master".
     8	---
     9	
    10	# PPT Master Skill
    11	
    12	> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.
    13	
    14	**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`
    15	
    16	> [!CAUTION]
    17	> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
    18	>
    19	> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
    20	>
    21	> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
    22	> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation. If no user is available (e.g. automated / non-interactive mode), the AI should make professional recommendations based on the source material and proceed automatically
    23	> 3. **NO CROSS-PHASE BUNDLING** — Cross-phase bundling is FORBIDDEN. (Note: the Eight Confirmations in Step 4 are ⛔ BLOCKING — the AI should present recommendations and seek user confirmation when possible. Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), all subsequent non-BLOCKING steps — design spec output, SVG generation, speaker notes, and post-processing — may proceed automatically without further confirmation)
    24	> 4. **GATE BEFORE ENTRY** — Each Step has prerequisites (🚧 GATE) listed at the top; these MUST be verified before starting that Step
    25	> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
    26	> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN
    27	> 7. **SEQUENTIAL PAGE GENERATION ONLY** — In Executor Step 6, after the global design context is confirmed, SVG pages MUST be generated sequentially page by page in one continuous pass. Grouped page batches (for example, 5 pages at a time) are FORBIDDEN
    28	
    29	> [!IMPORTANT]
    30	> ## 🌐 Language & Communication Rule
    31	>
    32	> - **Response language**: Always match the language of the user's input and provided source materials. For example, if the user asks in Chinese, respond in Chinese; if the source material is in English, respond in English.
    33	> - **Explicit override**: If the user explicitly requests a specific language (e.g., "请用英文回答" or "Reply in Chinese"), use that language instead.
    34	> - **Template format**: The `design_spec.md` file MUST always follow its original English template structure (section headings, field names), regardless of the conversation language. Content values within the template may be in the user's language.
    35	
    36	> [!IMPORTANT]
    37	> ## 🔌 Compatibility With Generic Coding Skills
    38	>
    39	> - `ppt-master` is a repository-specific workflow skill, not a general application scaffold
    40	> - Do NOT create or require `.worktrees/`, `tests/`, branch workflows, or other generic engineering structure by default
    41	> - If another generic coding skill suggests repository conventions that conflict with this workflow, follow this skill first unless the user explicitly asks otherwise
    42	
    43	## Main Pipeline Scripts
    44	
    45	| Script | Purpose |
    46	|--------|---------|
    47	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/pdf_to_md.py` | PDF to Markdown |
    48	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py` | Documents to Markdown via Pandoc (DOCX, EPUB, HTML, LaTeX, RST, etc.) |
    49	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.py` | Web page to Markdown |
    50	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.cjs` | WeChat / high-security sites to Markdown |
    51	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/project_manager.py` | Project init / validate / manage |
    52	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/analyze_images.py` | Image analysis |
    53	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/image_gen.py` | AI image generation (multi-provider) |
    54	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/svg_quality_checker.py` | SVG quality check |
    55	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/total_md_split.py` | Speaker notes splitting |
    56	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/finalize_svg.py` | SVG post-processing (unified entry) |
    57	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/svg_to_pptx.py` | Export to PPTX |
    58	
    59	For complete tool documentation, see `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/README.md`.
    60

    62	
    63	| Index | Path | Purpose |
    64	|-------|------|---------|

    66	| Chart templates | `${SKILL_DIR}/templates/charts/charts_index.json` | Query available chart SVG templates |

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Ethereum Supply Dynamics

#### Slide 01 — Cover

- **Layout**: Single column centered, dark background
- **Title**: Ultra Sound Money: Ethereum's Supply Dynamics & Monetary Thesis
- **Subtitle**: A data-driven analysis of post-merge ETH economics, burn mechanics, and long-term supply equilibrium
- **Info**: Current supply ~121.6M ETH | Gas ~0.1 Gwei | ETH ~$2,243 | April 2026
- **Chart**: None

#### Slide 02 — Supply Change Snapshot

- **Layout**: Top KPI cards + bottom grouped bar chart (left-right split 5:5)
- **Title**: ETH Supply Growing at +0.83%/Year with Only 192 ETH Burned in 7 Days
- **Chart**: grouped_bar_chart — issuance (19,638 ETH) vs burn (192 ETH)
- **Content**:
  - Total supply: 121,603,980 ETH
  - 7-day net change: +19,445.89 ETH
  - Issued: 19,638.29 ETH
  - Burned: 192.39 ETH
  - Offset ratio: 0.01x (burns offset only ~1% of issuance)
  - Annualized growth: +0.83%/year

#### Slide 03 — Gas and Burn Mechanics

- **Layout**: Left gauge chart + right data points
- **Title**: Base Gas at Historic Lows: 0.1 Gwei Average Suppresses Fee Burn
- **Chart**: gauge_chart — current 0.1 Gwei vs equilibrium 22 Gwei
- **Content**:
  - EIP-1559 burn mechanism: base fees destroyed
  - 7-day gas market: min 0.0, max 1.3, avg 0.1 Gwei
  - Blob gas (EIP-4844): avg ~7.1M wei, 0.15 ETH burned in 7 days
  - Equilibrium assumption: 22 Gwei (far above current)
  - Low gas = low burn = temporary supply inflation

#### Slide 04 — Burn Leaderboard Categories

- **Layout**: Left horizontal bar chart + right leaderboard table
- **Title**: DeFi and ETH Transfers Account for 85% of Weekly Fee Burn
- **Chart**: horizontal_bar_chart — burn categories (DeFi 31, ETH transfers 22, misc 4, NFTs 3, contracts 2, L2/MEV/blobs 0)
- **Content**:
  - Top burners: ETH transfers 21.74 ETH, Tether USDT 13.55 ETH
  - Recent blocks: 0.00–0.01 ETH per block
  - 7-day burn record: 0.07 ETH in a single block
  - Total 7-day burn: ~192 ETH

#### Slide 05 — Staking and Validator Economics

- **Layout**: Top KPI cards + bottom donut chart
- **Title**: 38.9M ETH Staked at 2.7% Issuance Rewards with Minimal Tips and MEV
- **Chart**: donut_chart — reward composition (issuance 2.7%, tips 0.1%, MEV 0.1%)
- **Content**:
  - 38.9M ETH staked (~32% of supply)
  - Scarcity engine: 9.1M ETH locked, avg 10.7 years
  - Validator rewards: issuance 0.9 ETH/val (2.7%), tips 0.0 ETH (0.1%), MEV 0.0 ETH (0.1%)
  - Total APR: ~2.9%
  - PoS issuance: ~2,800 ETH/day

#### Slide 06 — Supply Projections

- **Layout**: Full-width line chart + parameter cards below
- **Title**: Long-Term Equilibrium Projected at 125.7M ETH with 1,037K ETH/Year Issuance-Burn Balance
- **Chart**: line_chart — 200-year supply trajectory converging to 125.7M ETH
- **Content**:
  - Equilibrium: 125.7M ETH
  - Parameters: 39M ETH staked, 22 Gwei avg base gas
  - Balance: ~1,037K ETH/year issuance = burn
  - Staker rewards rate: 2.7%/year
  - Non-staker effective burn rate: 1.2%/year
  - Historical eras: genesis (5 ETH/block) → Byzantium (3) → Constantinople (2) → phase 0 → London burn → merge

#### Slide 07 — Flippening and Total Value Secured

- **Layout**: Top flippening metrics + bottom stacked bar chart
- **Title**: ETH at 18.7% of Bitcoin's Market Cap, Securing $272B in Native Value
- **Chart**: stacked_bar_chart — TVS composition (ETH $272.76B, ERC20s $22.21B, NFTs $12.66B)
- **Content**:
  - Flippening progress: BTC 18.70%, USD 1.30%, Gold 0.89%
  - Total Value Secured: ~$307.6B
  - Top ERC20s: Dai $4.41B, SHIB $3.51B, Cronos $2.97B, Tether Gold $2.65B
  - Top NFTs: CryptoPunks $2.13B, BAYC $0.68B, ENS $0.63B, Pudgy Penguins $0.51B
  - Community: 6,000+ members tracking metrics

#### Slide 08 — Key Takeaways

- **Layout**: Single column centered, 5 takeaway cards stacked
- **Title**: Key Takeaways: Ultra Sound Money Thesis Intact but Gas Activity Is the Critical Variable
- **Chart**: None
- **Content**:
  1. ETH is currently mildly inflationary at +0.83%/yr due to historically low gas (avg 0.1 Gwei)
  2. Burn mechanism works but requires sustained on-chain activity to offset issuance
  3. 38.9M ETH staked creates significant supply lock (avg 10.7 years)
  4. Long-term equilibrium at 125.7M ETH is structurally sound at 22 Gwei
  5. Flippening progress (18.7% of BTC) and $307B+ TVS demonstrate growing monetary premium
  - Forward-looking: ultra sound money thesis depends on on-chain activity recovery

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: Match SVG names (`01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
- **Content style**: Formal, data-interpretive, conclusion-first

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` (`<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN)
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`; `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN (group opacity); set on each child element individually
- Image transparency uses overlay mask layer (`<rect fill="bg-color" opacity="0.x"/>`)
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

     7	## Role Definition

Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
    14	
    15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
    16	
    17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
    18	|---------|---------|---------------|
    19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
    20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
    21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
    22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
    23	
    24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
    25	
    26	**Title writing**:
    27	
    28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
    29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
    30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
    31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
    32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
    33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
    34	
    35	---
    36	
    37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
    38	
    39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
    40	
    41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
    42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
    43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
    44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
    45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
    46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
    47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
    48	
    49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
    50	
    51	```xml
    52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
    53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
    54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
    55	```
    56	
    57	---
    58	
    59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
    60	
    61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
    62	
    63	```
    64	         ┌─────────────────┐
    65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
    66	         └────────┬────────┘
    67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
    68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
    69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
    70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
    71	```
    72	
    73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
    74	|-------|----------|-----------|
    75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
    76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
    77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

    79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

    93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
    94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
    95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
    96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
    97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
    98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
    99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
   100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
   101	```
   102	
   103	### Strategic Roadmap
   104	
   105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
   106	
   107	```
   108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
   109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
   110	```
   111	
   112	### Benchmarking Matrix
   113	
   114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
   115	
   116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
   117	
   118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
   119	
   120	---
   121	
   122	## Strategic Use of Color
   123	
   124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
   125	
   126	| Purpose | Method |
   127	|---------|--------|
   128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
   129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
   130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
   131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
   132	
   133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
   134	
   135	---
   136	
   137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
   138	
   139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
   140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
   141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
   142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
   143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
   144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
   145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
   146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
   147	
   148	---
   149	
   150	## Speaker Notes Style
   151	
   152	### Narrative Tone
   153	
   154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
   155	
   156	### Stage Direction Markers
   157	
   158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
   159	|--------|---------|---------|
   160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
   161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
   162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
   163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
   164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
   165	
   166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
   167	
   168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
   169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
   170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
   171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
   172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
   173	
   174	### Notes Example
   175	
   176	```markdown
   177	# 03_strategic_path
   178	
   179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
   180	
   181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
   182	
   183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
   184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
   185	
   186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
   187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
   188	
   189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
   190	
   191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
   192	Duration: 3 minutes
   193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
   194	```
   195	
   196	---
   197	
   198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
   199	
   200	### Content Level
   201	
   202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
   203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
   204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
   205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
   206	
   207	### Visual Level
   208	
   209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
   210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
   211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
   212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
   213	
   214	### Notes Level
   215	
   216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
   217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
   218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

# Speaker Notes — Ultra Sound Money: Ethereum's Post-Merge Supply Dynamics

---

## Slide 01: Cover

Welcome to this deep-dive analysis of Ethereum's post-Merge supply dynamics. Today we'll examine whether ETH truly lives up to its "ultra sound money" moniker, or if current on-chain data tells a more nuanced story. We'll cover supply mechanics, burn dynamics, staking concentration, long-term projections, and the ever-elusive "flippening."

---

## Slide 02: Supply Snapshot

The headline figure: Ethereum's total supply stands at approximately 121.6 million ETH, with a current market price of $2,243. Over the past 7 days, net supply increased by roughly 19,446 ETH. Here's the breakdown: issuance totaled about 19,638 ETH, while burn removed only 192 ETH. That gives us a burn-to-issuance offset ratio of just 0.01x — meaning only 1% of newly issued ETH is being burned. The key insight is that at current gas prices of 0.1 Gwei, burn is essentially negligible compared to issuance. This is a far cry from the post-Merge deflationary narrative.

---

## Slide 03: Gas Price & Burn Analysis

This slide visualizes the gas price equilibrium problem. The gauge shows current gas at 0.1 Gwei — barely registering on the scale — while equilibrium requires approximately 22 Gwei. At current levels, daily issuance of ~2,805 ETH is only offset by ~27 ETH in daily burn, creating net inflation of ~2,778 ETH per day. For Ethereum to become truly "ultrasound" — where burn exceeds issuance — gas prices need to sustain above 22 Gwei. During peak NFT and DeFi activity in 2021-2022, we routinely saw 50-100+ Gwei, but current L2 migration and reduced on-chain activity have suppressed base layer demand.

---

## Slide 04: Burn Leaderboard

The burn leaderboard reveals which protocols and activities are driving fee consumption. ETH transfers lead at roughly 120 ETH burned over 7 days, followed by Uniswap V3 at ~90 ETH and Tether transfers at ~60 ETH. Notably, OpenSea — once a dominant burner during the NFT boom — has fallen to ~30 ETH. The combined 7-day burn across all activities is only ~192 ETH total. For context, during peak bull market conditions, Ethereum burned over 10,000 ETH per day. The current low burn environment reflects both reduced speculative activity and successful L2 scaling diverting transactions away from L1.

---

## Slide 05: Staking Landscape

Approximately 38.9 million ETH is currently staked, representing about 32% of total supply. The donut chart shows this split against the 68% unstaked. On the provider breakdown, Lido dominates liquid staking with roughly 28% market share — about 10.9 million ETH. This concentration is noteworthy from a decentralization perspective. Coinbase follows at ~8%, Binance at ~6%, and Figment at ~4%. Solo stakers and smaller providers collectively make up the remaining ~51%. Current staking yield is approximately 3.2% APR, comprising consensus rewards and execution layer tips. The Lido concentration remains a key risk factor for network neutrality.

---

## Slide 06: Long-Term Supply Projections

This chart traces Ethereum's supply from genesis in 2015 through the present and projects the 200-year trajectory. Key historical eras: genesis started at 5 ETH per block, reduced to 3 ETH at Byzantium in 2017, then 2 ETH at Constantinople in 2019. The London upgrade in 2021 introduced EIP-1559 and the burn mechanism. The Merge in September 2022 replaced proof-of-work with proof-of-stake, cutting issuance by roughly 90%. Current supply is ~121.6 million, and the model projects asymptotic convergence toward an equilibrium of approximately 125.7 million ETH. The curve flattens significantly post-Merge, but the network is still net-inflationary at current activity levels.

---

## Slide 07: Flippening & TVS Analysis

Ethereum's market cap of approximately $307 billion represents about 18.7% of Bitcoin's market cap — the "flippening" ratio. The historical high for this ratio was around 50% in December 2021. Total Value Secured, which measures all assets relying on Ethereum for settlement security, breaks down as: ETH native at $272.76 billion or 88.7%, ERC-20 tokens at $22.21 billion or 7.2%, and NFTs at $12.66 billion or 4.1%. On the path to flippening: the bear case sees ETH losing share to L2s with the ratio falling below 10%; the base case envisions gradual convergence to 25-35% as ETH's monetary premium grows; the bull case requires Ethereum to become the dominant settlement layer, potentially achieving flippening within 5-10 years.

---

## Slide 08: Key Takeaways

To summarize: First, low gas prices mean Ethereum is currently inflationary, not deflationary — the "ultrasound" narrative only holds above ~22 Gwei. Second, staking concentration via Lido at 28% poses meaningful centralization risks. Third, long-term supply will asymptotically approach ~125.7 million ETH over roughly 200 years — the Merge slowed issuance dramatically but didn't eliminate it. Fourth, the flippening remains uncertain with ETH at just 18.7% of BTC's market cap; structural catalysts are needed for convergence. The strategic implication: Ethereum's value proposition has evolved from "ultrasound money" toward "world computer" — and investors should calibrate expectations accordingly.

Thank you. I'm happy to take questions.

---

    77	def build_match_maps(svg_stems: List[str]) -> Tuple[set, Dict[str, List[str]], Dict[int, List[str]]]:
    78	    exact = set(svg_stems)
    79	    norm_map: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
    80	    num_map: Dict[int, List[str]] = {}
    81	    for stem in svg_stems:
    82	        norm = normalize_title(stem)
    83	        if norm:
    84	            norm_map.setdefault(norm, []).append(stem)
    85	        num = extract_leading_number(stem)
    86	        if num is not None:
    87	            num_map.setdefault(num, []).append(stem)
    88	    return exact, norm_map, num_map

    91	def match_title(
    92	    raw_title: str,
    93	    exact: set,
    94	    norm_map: Dict[str, List[str]],
    95	    num_map: Dict[int, List[str]],
    96	    svg_stems: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    97	) -> Optional[str]:
    98	    if raw_title in exact:
    99	        return raw_title
   100	    norm = normalize_title(raw_title)
   101	    if norm in norm_map and len(norm_map[norm]) == 1:
   102	        return norm_map[norm][0]
   103	    num = extract_leading_number(raw_title)
   104	    if num is not None and num in num_map and len(num_map[num]) == 1:
   105	        return num_map[num][0]
   106	    if norm and svg_stems:
   107	        candidates = [s for s in svg_stems if norm in normalize_title(s)]
   108	        if len(candidates) == 1:
   109	            return candidates[0]
   110	    return None

   132	def parse_total_md(md_path: Path, svg_stems: Optional[List[str]] = None, verbose: bool = True) -> Dict[str, str]:
   133	    """
   134	    Parse total.md file and extract speaker notes content for each level-1 heading
   135	
   136	    Args:
   137	        md_path: Path to total.md file
   138	
   139	    Returns:
   140	        Dictionary where key is the level-1 heading (without #) and value is the notes content
   141	    """
   142	    if not md_path.exists():
   143	        print(f"Error: {md_path} file does not exist")
   144	        return {}
   145	
   146	    try:
   147	        with open(md_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
   148	            content = f.read()
   149	    except Exception as e:
   150	        print(f"Error: Unable to read file {md_path}: {e}")
   151	        return {}
   152	
   153	    svg_stems = svg_stems or []
   154	    exact, norm_map, num_map = build_match_maps(svg_stems)
   155	
   156	    # Parse by headings (supports # / ## / ###)
   157	    notes: Dict[str, str] = {}
   158	    current_key: Optional[str] = None
   159	    current_lines: List[str] = []
   160	    unmatched_headings: List[str] = []
   161	
   162	    lines = content.splitlines()
   163	    for line in lines:
   164	        m = HEADING_RE.match(line)
   165	        if m:
   166	            raw_title = m.group(2).strip()
   167	            matched = match_title(raw_title, exact, norm_map, num_map, svg_stems)
   168	            if matched:
   169	                if current_key is not None:
   170	                    text = '\n'.join(current_lines).strip()
   171	                    if current_key in notes and text:
   172	                        notes[current_key] = (notes[current_key].rstrip() + "\n\n" + text).strip()
   173	                    elif current_key not in notes:
   174	                        notes[current_key] = text
   175	                current_key = matched
   176	                current_lines = []
   177	                continue
   178	            unmatched_headings.append(raw_title)
   179	
   180	        if HR_RE.match(line):
   181	            continue
   182	        if current_key is not None:
   183	            current_lines.append(line)
   184	
   185	    if current_key is not None:
   186	        text = '\n'.join(current_lines).strip()
   187	        if current_key in notes and text:
   188	            notes[current_key] = (notes[current_key].rstrip() + "\n\n" + text).strip()
   189	        elif current_key not in notes:
   190	            notes[current_key] = text
   191	
   192	    if verbose and unmatched_headings:
   193	        print("\n[Notice] Found unmatched headings (ignored):")
   194	        for t in unmatched_headings[:10]:
   195	            print(f"  - {t}")
   196	        if len(unmatched_headings) > 10:
   197	            print(f"  ... and {len(unmatched_headings) - 10} more")
   198	
   199	    return notes

   202	def check_svg_note_mapping(svg_files: List[Path], notes: Dict[str, str]) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
   203	    """
   204	    Check the mapping between SVG files and speaker notes
   205	
   206	    Args:
   207	        svg_files: List of SVG files
   208	        notes: Notes dictionary (key is heading)
   209	
   210	    Returns:
   211	        (whether all matched, list of missing notes headings)
   212	    """
   213	    missing_notes = []
   214	
   215	    for svg_path in svg_files:
   216	        # Extract SVG filename (without extension)
   217	        svg_stem = svg_path.stem
   218	
   219	        # Check if a corresponding heading exists in the notes
   220	        if svg_stem not in notes:
   221	            missing_notes.append(svg_stem)
   222	
   223	    return len(missing_notes) == 0, missing_notes

   226	def split_notes(notes: Dict[str, str], output_dir: Path, verbose: bool = True) -> bool:
   227	    """
   228	    Split and save notes dictionary into multiple files
   229	
   230	    Args:
   231	        notes: Notes dictionary (key is heading, value is content)
   232	        output_dir: Output directory
   233	        verbose: Whether to output detailed information
   234	
   235	    Returns:
   236	        Whether successful
   237	    """
   238	    if not notes:
   239	        print("Error: No notes content found")
   240	        return False
   241	
   242	    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   243	
   244	    success_count = 0
   245	
   246	    for title, content in notes.items():
   247	        # Generate output filename (same name as SVG file, with .md extension)
   248	        output_path = output_dir / f"{title}.md"
   249	
   250	        try:
   251	            with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
   252	                f.write(content)
   253	
   254	            if verbose:
   255	                print(f"  Generated: {output_path.name}")
   256	
   257	            success_count += 1
   258	
   259	        except Exception as e:
   260	            if verbose:
   261	                print(f"  Error: Unable to write file {output_path}: {e}")
   262	
   263	    if verbose:
   264	        print(f"\n[Done] Successfully generated {success_count}/{len(notes)} file(s)")
   265	
   266	    return success_count == len(notes)

   274	Examples:
